definition: The Anglo-American Cataloguing Rules prescribe how to describe library materials and select access points in catalog records.
example: A cataloguer prepares a record that makes a book discoverable under its author and title.

definition: Angular CLI is a command-line tool for generating, building, testing, and maintaining Angular projects.
example: A developer generates an Angular component with a matching test file.

definition: Angular is a TypeScript-based framework for building web applications with components, declarative templates, and dependency injection.
example: A development team creates a dashboard whose components share a data service.

definition: AngularJS is the original JavaScript-based Angular framework that links HTML templates to application data and behavior through directives and binding.
example: A maintainer updates a form in a legacy AngularJS application.
sense_note: This is the earlier 1.x framework, not Angular 2 or later.

definition: Anim8or is a desktop application for polygonal 3D modeling and character animation.
example: An animator creates a simple model and poses it across keyframes.

definition: Animated explainer video production uses scripted narration and moving visuals to teach or explain a topic.
example: An instructional team animates a parcel’s route to explain a warehouse’s fulfillment process.

definition: Anma is a Japanese massage tradition using manual pressure, kneading, and related bodywork techniques.
example: A practitioner explains what an Anma session involves before agreeing on areas to address.

definition: Antics3D was a 3D animation and previsualization application for staging scenes with characters, sets, and camera moves.
example: A film planner blocks a scene and checks the planned camera framing before shooting.

definition: Antivirus software identifies and helps contain malicious programs or files through scanning and monitoring.
example: An endpoint agent quarantines a flagged attachment so a security team can review it.

definition: Apache Airflow orchestrates scheduled or triggered workflows whose tasks and dependencies are defined as directed acyclic graphs.
example: A data engineer makes a reporting task wait for two source extracts to complete.

definition: Apache Ambari is a tool for provisioning, managing, and monitoring Hadoop cluster services.
example: An administrator checks the health of distributed storage services across cluster nodes.

definition: Apache Ant is a Java-based build automation tool that executes targets and tasks commonly declared in XML.
example: A maintainer builds an application and packages the result using its existing Ant build file.

definition: Apache Archiva manages repositories of software build artifacts, particularly for Maven-based projects.
example: A build team serves approved dependency versions from an internal repository.

definition: Apache Beam defines batch and streaming data pipelines through a unified model that runs on supported processing back ends.
example: An engineer uses the same transformation logic for historical records and newly arriving events.

definition: Apache Cassandra is a distributed wide-column database designed to store and serve large datasets across multiple nodes.
example: A service stores device readings by device identifier and time window.

definition: Apache Cocoon is a web application framework that processes and transforms content through pipelines, historically centered on XML.
example: A publisher transforms structured documents into web pages using a series of content-processing stages.

definition: Apache Giraph is a distributed graph-processing framework that runs iterative computations over graph vertices and edges.
example: An analyst computes connected components in a large relationship network.

definition: Apache Gump is a continuous integration system that builds related open-source projects to detect dependency and compatibility problems.
example: A project maintainer sees that a change in an upstream library breaks a downstream build.

definition: Apache Jena is a Java framework for RDF data, SPARQL queries, and semantic-web applications.
example: A research team queries a graph of collections and the people connected to them.

definition: Apache jUDDI is a Java implementation of the UDDI registry standard for publishing and discovering web services.
example: An enterprise maintains a searchable registry of service descriptions for internal applications.

definition: Apache Karaf is a modular Java runtime for deploying and managing OSGi applications and related components.
example: An operator enables a packaged feature without rebuilding the surrounding application runtime.

definition: Apache Lenya is a web content-management system built around XML documents and publication workflows.
example: An editor reviews and publishes a structured article through the site’s approval process.

definition: Apache Mahout provides scalable mathematical and machine-learning tools for processing large datasets.
example: An analyst applies distributed computation to a large feature matrix.

definition: Apache Mesos manages and allocates shared compute resources to distributed workload frameworks.
example: A cluster operator runs multiple processing frameworks on a common pool of machines.

definition: Apache NiFi designs and operates data flows for moving, routing, and transforming data between systems.
example: A team routes incoming sensor records to different destinations according to their source.

definition: Apache ObJectRelationalBridge is a Java object-relational mapping tool for persisting object data in relational databases.
example: A maintainer maps an application’s order objects to tables without writing SQL for every save.

definition: Apache OFBiz is a framework and suite of enterprise applications for functions such as order management, accounting, and commerce.
example: A retailer connects its product catalog and fulfillment records in a shared system.

definition: Apache OpenEJB is an implementation of the Enterprise JavaBeans container specification for running enterprise Java components.
example: A developer runs transaction-aware application services in an embedded container during tests.

definition: Apache OpenNLP is a Java toolkit for common statistical natural language processing tasks such as tokenization and named entity recognition.
example: A developer identifies person and organization names in a collection of articles.

definition: Apache PDFBox is a Java library for creating, reading, and manipulating PDF documents.
example: A developer extracts searchable text from incoming PDF forms.

definition: Apache PredictionIO was a platform for building and deploying machine-learning prediction services.
example: A team wraps a recommendation model as an application-facing prediction service.

definition: Apache Spark is a distributed computation engine for large-scale data processing and analytics.
example: A team aggregates months of event records across a cluster.

definition: Apache Tiles is a Java web presentation framework for composing pages from reusable layout fragments.
example: A team shares navigation and footer fragments across several web pages.

definition: Apache TinkerPop is a graph computing framework that defines common interfaces and the Gremlin traversal language.
example: A developer uses Gremlin to find connections between people and projects.

definition: API design defines an interface’s operations, data contracts, and behavior so callers can use it reliably.
example: A team specifies how an orders API responds to duplicate requests and invalid input.

definition: An API gateway is an entry point that routes API requests and can apply common controls before forwarding them to back-end services.
example: A gateway authenticates a request before routing it to the product service.

definition: API management governs the publication, access, monitoring, and evolution of APIs across their lifecycle.
example: A platform team tracks usage and communicates the retirement date of an old API version.

definition: Apollo GraphQL is a set of tools for building, consuming, and operating GraphQL APIs.
example: A web app uses Apollo Client to fetch and cache data for its account page.

definition: Appian is a low-code software platform for building workflow and process applications.
example: An operations team creates a claims review workflow with different steps for intake and approval.

definition: Apple Device Enrollment Program was an Apple service for automating institutional enrollment of eligible devices into mobile device management.
example: A school sets up new iPads to enroll automatically during initial setup.
sense_note: The historical DEP label should not be used interchangeably with every current Apple device management service.
